note: The operator brought in an outside physics paper -- 'Ping World: A Toy Derivation of Relativistic Consequences' by u/alamalarian, which derives special relativity from a pure signalling model: observers that know each other only through finite-speed pings, with every measurable quantity derived from received ping counts. A conceptual line-up with the fleet was proposed in chat (Rule II's ordered, gap-free, append-only 'faithful record' as the same object as Nestor's append-only ledger; 'observation requires received pings' as the same epistemology as 'Has a human checked this?' and remote-to-local). To test the proposal rather than assert it, the paper was fed through Nestor two ways: a fresh store built from ten of its claims in the paper's own words, and those same claims matched against the box's decision store (docs/dogfood/nestor.db). The operator has a fuller study of the paper still local, not in the vault.

decisions.question: Fed Ping World's ten claims through Nestor -- on their own and against the box's 294-decision store -- to test a proposed cross-domain line-up. What did Nestor return?
decisions.commitment: Not served, and honestly so. Against the box store every claim scored 0.41-0.48 under the character StringMatcher -- below the 0.92 serve bar and mostly below the 0.45 calibrated knee -- and the top matches were function-word / question-shape noise, not concept: the 'faithful record is ordered, gap-free' claim's nearest was 'Why did Round 2 produce a document rather than a script?' at 0.412, not any ledger decision. On its own the paper's claims sat 0.32-0.42 apart, distinct to the matcher, the single strongest internal link riding only on the shared word 'absolute'. The semantic matcher that could cross vocabularies is unreachable in this box (SemanticMatcher needs the 'semantic' extra; the embedder backends are egress-blocked, decision 0084). So Nestor returned unknown, not 'no line-up', and the proposed correspondence stays an unsealed proposal.
decisions.why: A near miss served as verified is worse than no answer, and absence surfaces as unknown rather than as a result -- Nestor declining to dress a 0.455 character collision as a match is that first law in action, not a failure of the run. A genuine cross-domain paraphrase (same concept, near-zero shared vocabulary) is exactly the semantic tail the N1 bench and the matcher-precision gate identified, here in its purest form: the character matcher can rank but cannot bridge vocabularies, so a real conceptual isomorphism scores like noise. The experiment therefore measured Nestor's own boundary, and found the interesting correspondence living precisely on the far side of it.

decisions.question: Is the Ping World / fleet correspondence itself recorded here as a fact?
decisions.commitment: No -- as a draft proposal with its measurement attached, unsealed. The machine proposed the line-up (faithful-record = ledger; received-signal epistemology = the seal covenant) and Nestor will not confirm it from character overlap. Only the semantic matcher (unavailable in this box) or a human sealing in nestor ui can adjudicate it.
decisions.why: This is the paper's own closing move mapped onto the covenant: a fork between two internally consistent readings cannot be settled by argument, only by observation. The observation Nestor can make (character similarity) does not settle it; the observation that could (semantic distance) cannot run here. So the disposition is the honest one -- propose, do not confirm -- and the correspondence waits for an instrument or a human, which is where every unsealed claim in this store waits.
